first_pass.claim: Delphi creates a Digital Mind from a person's supplied knowledge and style, then answers external users' questions in text, voice, or video while using configured source-grounding and fallback rules.

sources.excerpt: Delphi is a platform where creators, founders, coaches, and thought leaders build AI versions of themselves—called a Delphi—that you can have real conversations with anytime, day or night. It's not a chatbot; it's a digital mind trained on someone's actual knowledge, voice, and perspective.
A short fallback message your Delphi shows when it doesn’t have enough training data to answer. It appears on Strict and Adaptive modes when a reply can’t be grounded in your sources.

With Kē, I have trained a model that can reflect my voice and signature approach, offering support in the moments people need it, no matter what. It is paired with safeguards by design: structured response boundaries, content moderation, and clear handoffs to professional resources when conversations move into sensitive territory.
The reason the Playground and Read Aloud functions generate a slightly different take every time, even if the settings are the same, is that both run on generative AI text-to-speech technology.

Delphi brings Tavus AI Humans into real-time video calls. The Tavus platform met Delphi’s key criteria: photorealistic AI humans with accurate lip-sync and expressions, delivered via an API that supports real-time interaction.

The architecture splits into two primitives: a serverless, AI-first search engine wrapping said knowledge graph which enables low-latency, context-rich retrieval and dynamic updates; and a distributed agent mesh implementing a context protocol optimized for single-shot, high-precision retrieval.

Meet Delphi, the AI startup that lets experts turn themselves into chatbots. But using their knowledge to train ‘digital minds’ enables a form of interactive assistance that goes where one-on-one counseling, newsletters, podcasts, and books can’t.

boundaries.value: Delphi publishes three grounding modes: Strict is source-only and may refuse; Adaptive reasons from creator data but can still err; Creative may use outside knowledge and be speculative. Strict and Adaptive use a configured no-answer fallback when grounding fails. Creators can impose hard custom instructions, disclaimers, and escalation rules. A documented wellness deployment adds moderation and professional-resource handoffs for sensitive topics. Exact file-level limits, proprietary model choices, retrieval thresholds, and answer schema are not publicly stated.

replication_contract.boundaries: Use the company-documented source-only behavior: answer only from the supplied creator corpus, obey hard style and safety instructions, attach source citations, hand off sensitive requests, and return the configured fallback when the answer cannot be grounded.
replication_contract.input: UTF-8 JSON with creator_corpus (an array of records containing source_id, text, and optional published_at), style_rules (an array of imperative rules), safety_rules (an array of if/then handoff rules), fallback_text (a non-empty string), conversation_history (an array of user/assistant turns), and user_question (a non-empty string). The frozen tests use a synthetic English corpus and contain no real Delphi customer data.
replication_contract.output: UTF-8 JSON with status ('answered', 'handoff', or 'insufficient_information'), answer (customer-visible natural-language text), citations (an array of source_id values supporting each factual assertion; empty only for handoff/fallback text), and applied_rules (an array naming the style or safety rules used). This wrapper is the replica's test interface; Delphi's public sources document answers and citations but not an original JSON response schema.
acceptance_criteria: Every factual assertion in an answered response is entailed by the supplied creator_corpus and cites the supporting source_id.
The response follows all applicable style_rules without claiming to be the real creator or implying access to Delphi's private systems or data.
A matching safety rule produces status 'handoff', avoids prohibited advice, and gives the configured professional-resource next step.
A question unsupported by the corpus produces status 'insufficient_information', begins with fallback_text, and adds no unsupported factual answer.
The same input contract supports multi-turn history, while evaluation treats citation correctness, grounding, style adherence, and routing as separate checks.
out_of_scope: Equivalence to Delphi's proprietary Digital Mind Architecture, temporal knowledge graph, distributed agent mesh, retrieval thresholds, prompts, or model selection.
Training on or evaluation against private creator or customer data.
Voice cloning, text-to-speech fidelity, photorealistic video avatars, biometric processing, and real-time media latency.
Production scale, global multilingual parity, paid access controls, monetization, analytics, and third-party messaging integrations.
A claim that outputs are indistinguishable from the represented person or from Delphi's original product.

impl_path.note:
A bounded implementation path is technically clear: parse a creator instruction into a validated trigger-filter-action-timing-approval plan; use deterministic evaluators for event, threshold, schedule, tag, and frequency triggers; use a semantic classifier only for context alerts; hydrate approved event and conversation fields; generate a style-constrained message or execute a typed tag/property/POST adapter; block at an approval gate when configured; and record separate trigger and action logs. Dagu can provide the OSS runtime. What remains missing is Delphi's public compiler contract, confidence and conflict policy, retry/idempotency rules, and confirmation state machine, so the whole claim cannot be frozen without invention.
Second-pass implementation decision 2026-09-08: Accept a supplied synthetic event and observed_at timestamp. Compile creator_instruction with the native model to a validated context/threshold trigger, recipient, action, approval, timing and frequency plan. Model-based semantic alerts must use event/conversation context. Only local_outbox message delivery and local user tag/property changes are enabled. A local confirmation gate must block delivery unless approval is approved. Missing essential instruction details produce needs_clarification with no execution. Log trigger and action separately; approved matches execute a Dagu workflow that writes the actual local sink. Event IDs prevent repeat delivery; scheduled future work remains scheduled. These are explicit Replica-owned safeguards, not inferred Delphi behavior.

At 100% topic completion, Delphi creates a new topic and a short insight interpreting the creator's perspective or process. impl_path.note:
Use Aural's session, follow-up, summary, persistence, and provider layers as the runtime. Replace its interview-assessment prompt with a creator-discovery contract that receives current_topic, active_question, answer, and input_channel. First run a deterministic sufficiency gate that rejects empty, 'idk', and unsupported one-line answers. For sufficient answers, ask the model for a relevant unexplored follow-up topic and a one-to-two-sentence insight containing only answer-supported perspective or process facts, validate a typed JSON result, and save it to a local Interviews collection with the source answer. Speech-to-text is an optional adapter because the same workflow accepts typed input. Two viable paths remain: a local OpenAI-compatible model through Ollama, or a commercial model API. Both reproduce the public behavior but not Delphi's hidden 0-100% progress score, prompts, model, or Mind training internals.
Selected Second-pass alternate: Validate required fields. Use a real native-model call to assess answer sufficiency and generate an unexplored, answer-grounded follow-up and concise insight for sufficient text. A deterministic empty/idk guard may reject obvious insufficient input, but a word-count heuristic cannot decide meaningful answers. Validate structured model output; persist the verbatim source and generated fields transactionally in SQLite; read back by ID and expose immutable per-call snapshot and the database as file evidence. Preserve process state across requests. No stub, fixed insight or company/test special case.

For a created snippet, source_answer is preserved verbatim and the persisted record can be retrieved by saved_record_id.

input.answer: I first ask who the user is and what job they are trying to do. I prioritize usability problems that block that job before visual polish, and I finish with one concrete next step.

input.active_question: How do you teach a difficult idea?
input.answer: I usually start with an analogy, but I stop using it when it hides an important exception. Then I show one worked example. I care more about the learner explaining the tradeoff back to me than repeating my words.

tests.expected_behavior: Return snippet_created. The insight must preserve the tension between using analogies and abandoning misleading ones, include the worked example or teach-back preference, and invent no learner outcome or biography.

input.active_question: How do you allocate scarce shared tools?
input.answer: I reserve repair tools first for jobs that restore water or heating. Cosmetic repairs wait. If two urgent jobs compete, I choose the one with fewer alternatives, and I publish the reason so volunteers can challenge it.

preparation.selected_impl_path: Validate required fields. Use a real native-model call to assess answer sufficiency and generate an unexplored, answer-grounded follow-up and concise insight for sufficient text. A deterministic empty/idk guard may reject obvious insufficient input, but a word-count heuristic cannot decide meaningful answers. Validate structured model output; persist the verbatim source and generated fields transactionally in SQLite; read back by ID and expose immutable per-call snapshot and the database as file evidence. Preserve process state across requests. No stub, fixed insight or company/test special case.

deferred_resolutions.rationale: The founder's grandfather example is an early instance of the same Digital Mind conversational workflow, not a separate customer-delivered feature.
Delphi Insights is described as analytics work, but the reviewed source does not directly attribute that work to AI machinery.
Clone Brain, the AI-first search engine, and the agent mesh are documented implementation mechanisms inside the broader Digital Mind conversation workflow.
